cards.text: Friend, Jeremiah the prophet gets another word from the LORD, and this one's about Egypt. Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, is coming to strike the land of Egypt. And the LORD says don't keep it quiet: announce it in Egypt, in Migdol, in Memphis and in Tahpanhes.

cards.question: The LORD wants the news announced in Migdol, Memphis and Tahpanhes, because the sword devours those around them. What does the message tell Egypt to do?

answers.text: Take your positions and prepare yourself
Open your gates and welcome the king
Lay down your weapons and rest awhile

cards.text: Then the LORD asks a question. Why have Egypt's warriors been laid low? They can't even STAND.

cards.question: Egypt's warriors can't stand, because the ___ has thrust them down.

cards.text: They keep stumbling, and they fall right over one another. That's the whole office hitting the one elevator at five o'clock on a Friday.

cards.question: Egypt's stumbling warriors say to each other, Get up, let's go. True or false: they want to go back to their own people and the land of their birth.

cards.text: And there, they'll cry out about the man in charge: Pharaoh king of Egypt.

cards.question: When the warriors cry out about Pharaoh king of Egypt, what do they say about him?

answers.text: He was all noise and let his time pass
He fought for them to the very end
He sent them help right on time

cards.text: All noise. Like the dead batteries I shared that junk drawer with, swearing they had charge left and never powering a THING. Then the King speaks, whose name is the LORD of Hosts.

cards.question: The King, the LORD of Hosts, says someone is coming who stands out like Tabor among the mountains. True or false: the LORD swears to it by His own life.

cards.text: So someone's coming who stands out like Tabor among the mountains and Carmel by the sea. And Memphis, one of the towns that got the announcement, will be laid waste, destroyed and uninhabited.

cards.question: With Memphis about to be destroyed, the LORD tells the daughter dwelling in Egypt to pack her bags for ___.

cards.text: Then the LORD paints a picture, and Egypt is the star of it. Egypt is a beautiful heifer.

cards.question: Egypt is a beautiful heifer. What does the LORD say is coming against her from the north?

cards.text: A beautiful heifer versus a BUG, and friend, I have personally lost that fight to one fly in my bakery. Even the mercenaries among her are like fattened calves.

cards.question: The day of calamity is coming on Egypt, the time of punishment. True or false: the mercenaries among her will stand their ground.

cards.text: The enemy will advance in force against Egypt. And Egypt is going to make a sound.

cards.question: As the enemy advances, Egypt will hiss like a fleeing ___.

cards.text: With axes they'll come against her, like woodsmen cutting down trees. They'll chop down her forest, dense though it may be.

cards.question: Egypt's forest is dense, but the woodsmen chop it down anyway. Why can they?

answers.text: They are more numerous than locusts
They set the whole forest on fire
The trees have already dried out

cards.text: More than locusts, too many to count, and I can't even count the chocolate chips in ONE batch. The Daughter of Egypt will be put to shame.

cards.question: The Daughter of Egypt will be delivered into the hands of the people of the ___.

cards.text: Now the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel, gets specific. He's about to punish Amon, god of Thebes, along with Pharaoh, and Egypt with her gods and kings.

cards.question: Besides Amon, Pharaoh, and Egypt's gods and kings, the LORD names one more group. True or false: those who trust in Pharaoh will be punished too.

cards.text: He'll deliver them into the hands of those who seek their lives: Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon and his officers. But the LORD isn't done talking about Egypt.

cards.question: After Egypt is handed over to Nebuchadnezzar and his officers, what does the LORD say comes next for Egypt?

answers.text: It will be inhabited as in days of old
It will stay empty for all time
It will be covered over by the sea

cards.text: Egypt gets lived in again, and friend, a stamper who got pulled out of a junk drawer does NOT argue with a comeback. Then the LORD turns to Israel, His servant Jacob.

cards.question: Egypt was told to pack its bags. What does the LORD tell Jacob, His servant?

cards.text: The LORD says He will surely save Jacob out of a distant place, and Jacob's descendants from the land of their captivity.

cards.question: Once the LORD saves them, Jacob will return to ___ and ___, with no one to make him afraid.

cards.text: Then the LORD says it again to His servant Jacob: do not be afraid. Twice in a row, friend. When God repeats Himself, lean in.

cards.question: The second time the LORD tells Jacob not to be afraid, what reason does He give?

cards.text: The nations where the LORD banished Jacob? He will completely destroy them. Jacob? NOT completely.

cards.question: The LORD won't completely destroy Jacob. True or false: He says He will leave Jacob with no discipline at all.

findings.problem: The question says the LORD wants the news announced because the sword devours those around them. In Jeremiah 46:14, the clause 'for the sword devours those around you' gives the reason to take positions and prepare. It is not the reason for the announcement. The card adds a reason the text doesn't give and connects two things the text doesn't connect.

rule.text: Reasons: He never adds why someone did, said or thought something unless the text says why.

findings.problem: The joke compares the warriors to an office crowding the elevator at five o'clock on a Friday, which is everyone rushing to go home. That hints at the answer to card 6, which asks whether the warriors want to go back to their own people and the land of their birth (Jeremiah 46:16).

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: The question says the coming one 'stands out like Tabor among the mountains.' Jeremiah 46:18 says only 'one who is like Tabor among the mountains and like Carmel by the sea.' The text doesn't say how he is like Tabor, so 'stands out' adds an interpretation of the comparison.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: The card repeats 'someone's coming who stands out like Tabor among the mountains and Carmel by the sea.' Jeremiah 46:18 says only that he is like Tabor and like Carmel. The text doesn't say how he is like them, so 'stands out' adds an interpretation.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: The right answer 'exile' is a condition, but the wrong answers 'Jerusalem' and 'Thebes' are place names. The right answer stands out as the only one of its kind.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: The question says 'The day of calamity is coming on Egypt.' Jeremiah 46:21 says the day of calamity is 'coming upon them,' and 'them' means the mercenaries. The card changes who the text says the calamity comes on.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: Stop 1 card 14 already told the baker that the attacker comes 'from the north' (Jeremiah 46:20). That gives away this card's blank, 'people of the ___' with the answer 'north' (Jeremiah 46:24). The detail repeats in the passage, so it should only be asked the first time it appears.

rule.text: When a line repeats, like a psalm's refrain, ask about it only the first time it appears.

findings.problem: The question says 'Egypt was told to pack its bags.' Jeremiah 46:19 says 'Pack your bags for exile, O daughter dwelling in Egypt!' The text doesn't say who the daughter dwelling in Egypt is. Calling her Egypt settles something the text leaves open. Stop 1 card 12 used the text's own words correctly.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.
